newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest hits high as chemicals, energy shrs rise.
newsitem.headline: Budapest hits high as chemicals, energy shrs rise.

text.p: The Budapest Stock Exchange joined the group of firming foreign bourses and led by chemical and energy firms the index hit a new high, traders said.
The BUX index ended at 3,608.01 points, up 56.89, more than offsetting Thursday's loss of 30.14 points. The previous high of 3,581.26 points was reached on October 2.

"Buying mood on foreign markets spread over here," said Attila Gazdik of New York Broker Budapest. "Not only the Dow rises continously but London and other markets, too, as fresh capital flows into shares," he said.
Chemical firms came to focus on Friday enjoying the beneficial impact of rising PVC prices, traders said.
Borsodchem, however, was also propelled by its announcement of the purchase of a company in Austria.
Borsodchem firmed 100 forints from its 2,860 forint opening price to a daily peak of 2,960, but edged down to end at 2,955.
TVK broke out from its most recent price range around 1,350 forints and after firming to a daily high of 1,390 it ended at 1,375 forints, up 20.
Oil company MOL firmed almost five percent or 75 forints to end at 1,615 and while the market left investors in a bullish mood traders saw chances for some profit-taking.

The market has received little impetus from the corporate side until recently but more incentives were likely near the end of the month when companies in the listed A category will begin to publish their third quarter results.
